packageRules.description: Off by default, for two different reasons. The `actions/*` steps are deliberately on moving majors — they are published by GitHub itself, which is already the trust root for the runner, so a mutable tag there buys convenience without widening the supply chain. And `12-apps/ci`'s own `@v2` self-references are the moving major this repo PUBLISHES; a bot that pinned those would freeze the engine against itself.

The six third-party actions pinned to a full commit SHA. Every one of them either HANDLES a credential (docker/login-action takes the GHCR password, wrangler-action takes CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, build-push-action is handed SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN as BuildKit secrets) or runs in a job that does. A mutable tag lets the publisher retarget it at code nobody here reviewed, and because these sit in the shared engine that retarget reaches every consumer at once. Pinning removes that; this rule is what stops the pin becoming a freeze. Renovate rewrites the SHA and the trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment together, so the comment stays true. Grouped into one PR, reviewed and merged by a human — no automerge: the whole point is that a human sees what the new commit contains before every consumer runs it.
